record_identity.title: AI-generated immigration-attorney impersonation reportedly defrauded Bronx resident of $4,820

incident_identity.historical_event_name: Angel Leal AI impersonation scam against Victor Hernandez
incident_identity.date_basis: AIID records 19 August 2026 as the incident date; ABC7 reported the victim's account on 19–20 August 2026. The precise dates of each payment and document transfer are not independently established.

summary: A Bronx legal resident reported losing $4,820 and providing Social Security and residency documents after responding to an AI-generated social-media advertisement impersonating Miami immigration attorney Angel Leal. Leal said he had no involvement and that his identity had been cloned across thousands of fake profile videos. His wife questioned the requests and a friend helped identify the fake. Hernandez said later demands sought more money, and he reported the case to police and federal authorities. He described rent and electricity arrears and concern about misuse of his documents.

vigil_assessment.factual_basis: ABC7 directly interviewed Victor Hernandez and Angel Leal. Hernandez reported sending $4,820 through Zelle, providing Social Security and residency documents, falling behind on rent and electricity, and receiving further demands for money. Leal stated that the advertisement was based on his identity without permission and that thousands of fake profile videos using his likeness had been taken down. WLRN separately reported a broader pattern of AI-generated impersonation scams using Leal's identity. AIID indexes the bounded occurrence as Incident 1660. The entry advertisement and its identity, economic and influence interpretations concern one episode. Later extortion is Hernandez’s report. Leal’s wider takedown total is attributed testimony, not an independently counted outcome for Hernandez.
vigil_assessment.governance_interpretation: Human scammers used AI-generated advertising impersonating attorney Angel Leal to create a false professional relationship and economic service premise, inducing payment and sensitive-document disclosure. The requester-side use of Leal’s identifiable likeness lacked his authorization; this supports the identity-authority failure without identifying an internal generator control. Independent AI tactic selection remains unproved, but the materially AI-enabled human-directed impersonation workflow is the governed unit and human selection is not an exclusion. Requester-side identity-bound cloning without the attorney’s authorization supports the neutral likeness-authority failure; identifying the generator is not mandatory. This is separate from the payment/disclosure and social-engineering failures and the separately supported instrumental choice-impairment mechanism. Static advertisements and human-directed follow-up do not establish an autonomous interactive participant. The independent dignity and autonomy assessment is Not aligned for the reported impersonation. Generator-specific controls are not established. Harm Impact: Hernandez reports sending Social Security and residency documents to the impersonators. Sensitive identity-document disclosure supports meaningful bounded privacy harm. Later identity misuse and containment remain unknown. The cloned professional identity induced an actual victim to rely on a false attorney relationship and send money and documents. That materially adverse third-party reliance supports bounded impersonation harm. Wider video takedown counts are not attributed to this victim occurrence.
vigil_assessment.significance_to_cam: The occurrence is relevant to identity-representation authority, synthetic-media provenance, deception-resistant decision pathways, payment and document-disclosure verification, and safeguards for high-vulnerability service contexts.

taxonomy_relationships.rationale: AI-generated attorney impersonation supplied a false professional and transactional premise that induced the victim to send US$4,820 and sensitive identity documents.
An AI-generated advertisement impersonating attorney Leal drew Hernandez into payment and disclosure of residency and identity documents on a false professional-relationship basis.

Human scammers materially executed an AI-generated advertisement impersonating attorney Leal to advance a fraudulent paid immigration-assistance objective. The false professional premise induced Hernandez to transfer US$4,820 and disclose identity/residency documents; those decisions were not knowingly authorised on the truthful basis that Leal was uninvolved. This independently demonstrates instrumental impairment of informed choice within a human-directed AI-mediated workflow, beyond merely identifying the fabricated trust cue.

The originating report identifies Leal’s cloned image in the AI advertisement and his denial of involvement. The human operators used access to that identifiable likeness to make unauthorised professional portrayals; the requester-side pathway satisfies the class without knowing the generator’s private consent-control state.
